messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT PAGE: KV cache anomaly detected — continuous-batching rate spike. Alerting eng-sre and eng-oncall. https://incidents.redwood.example/INC-2026-2189990000 :pager:
Maria G.: paging — seeing sudden KV memory growth correlated with continuous-batching window changes. CPU on serving nodes climbing, eviction thrash.
Sam (sre_lead): copying. @Devon can you pull the heatmap and the per-tenant eviction rates?
Devon P.: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/kv/cache-ops?from=-30m to=now — spike starts ~10m ago. top offenders: tenant(acme-retail), tenant(bookflow), tenant-alpha.
Devon P.: snippet of query: `sum by(tenant) (kv_evictions{job=\"kv\"} - kv_evictions offset 5m)` shows 4x normal for those tenants.
Ashok: looks like the batch_config change we rolled last night increased batch size default for small requests — we mis-modeled seq length. continuous batching is coalescing too aggressively, causing hot prefix reuse and cache amplification.
Kelly (oncall): customer impact? are we seeing 5xx or latency spikes exposed to customers?
Jess C (support): support queue has 3 tickets from ACME and a post from enterprise dashboard showing 503s and request timeouts. They reported failures starting ~09:12 UTC.
Ryan M (prod): ACME is on Dedicated reservation w/ custom batching override; but our routing fingerprinting pushed some traffic to the new pathway after the rollout. They saw request tail-latency > 3s and some timeouts.
Sam (sre_lead): mitigation plan: 1) immediate per-tenant override for the top 3 offenders to reduce batching to previous safe values, 2) global partial rollback of the batch flag to reduce aggregation for small seqs, 3) start a canary with adjusted batch profile for low-traffic tenant to validate. who will run the per-tenant toggle?
Maria G.: I can do per-tenant toggles. Command (internal):
```
# set batch profile back for a tenant
curl -XPOST -H \"Authorization: Bearer $SRE_TOKEN\" \
  https://config.redwood.example/api/v1/tenants/acme-retail/overrides \
  -d '{"batch_size":"legacy-small","continuous_batching":false}'
```
Maria G.: will apply to acme-retail, bookflow, tenant-alpha now.
deploy-bot: config change queued: override for acme-retail by maria-g commit f3b2a9 — started.
Devon P.: applying override to first tenant — metric watch: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/kv/cache-ops?panel=evictions&orgId=1 — starting to see eviction rate drop for acme-retail.
Maria G.: acme override applied, eviction rate down 70% and tail-latency normalizing — removing from urgent list. :thumbsup:
Sam (sre_lead): good. Next global action — do we flip the batch flag off globally or do a staged canary? I prefer staged: roll 10% traffic to adjusted profile.
Ashok: we should do per-customer rollback for any tenant that still shows problems, then do canary with a smaller batch window (200ms instead of 500ms). I'll prepare the canary profile.
Kelly (oncall): can we do an emergency global flag off if more tenants degrade? we may need to move faster.
Sam (sre_lead): agree. threshold: if >5 tenants exceed eviction alert within 15m or any P0 customer timeouts persist, flip global flag to safe mode.
Devon P.: starting canary: applying new profile to `canary-tenant-001` at 09:36 UTC for 10% traffic. Monitoring dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/kv/canary-run
deploy-bot: canary rollout started — route change id: r-9843b — logs: https://deploys.redwood.example/r-9843b
Jess C (support): looping in Carina (CSM) to prepare customer comms. Carina, ACME already opened a ticket; they want ETA.
Carina (csm): on it — telling ACME we're investigating and applying targeted config changes. Will send a short note: \"We've applied a tenant-specific update to reduce inference batching while we validate a safer global config; monitoring indicates improved behavior for affected customers.\"
Sam (sre_lead): monitoring window 10m from canary start. If no regressions, we will expand to 30% and continue. If we see any regrowth in evictions, we abort and flip global safe flag.
Maria G.: canary 10% health after 6m: latency stable, no eviction spike. expanding to 30% now.
Devon P.: watch: bookflow still elevated — applying per-tenant override to bookflow now.
Maria G.: bookflow override applied; evictions trending down.
Sam (sre_lead): status check: acme-ok, bookflow-ok, tenant-alpha pending. we continue canary expansion.
Kelly (oncall): I'm going to coordinate on-call handoff in 20m to Ashok for postmortem + follow-up. I'll also create an incident slack channel and add the PM/CSM.
Sam (sre_lead): good call. After stabilizing, we need a postmortem with timeline, root cause (batch size modeling), and an action item: add a per-change canary pipeline for batch profile changes + automatic per-tenant rollout protection.
Carina (csm): communications for ACME sent. they acknowledged and appreciate the targeted rollback.
deploy-bot: config changes completed: overrides applied for acme-retail, bookflow, tenant-alpha. canary expansion steps recorded under r-9843b.
Kelly (oncall): Handoff to Ashok in 20m. I'll pile up the metrics, incident page, and the applied overrides in the new incident channel. tagging @pager-duty.
Ashok: taking post-handoff oncall. I'll own the follow-ups: perf regression reproduction, quant analysis, and next-day postmortem doc.
Sam (sre_lead): thanks everyone. summary: per-tenant overrides applied, canary validated, global rollback reserved as emergency measure. No additional P0 escalations. Moving to monitoring and comms phase.
Maria G.: noting commands used and timestamps on incident page.
Jess C (support): closing duplicate support tickets after ACME confirmation.
Carina (csm): will follow up with customers after final stabilizing window.
Kelly (oncall): final note before handoff — if you see new regression signals, call the incident channel and we will immediate flip the global safe flag. :rotating_light:
